governanceNotes: D1 batch 77 (2026-09-26): two bounded association edges authored - raynaud-s-phenomenon to depressive-disorder (rank 1) and anxiety-disorder (rank 2) - both classified ASSOCIATION_ONLY with etiologicalConsensus NOT_ESTABLISHED, vaNexusProbabilityAlignment NOT_ASSERTED, and hypothesizedOnly:true. The edges rest on the controlled primary-Raynaud cohort of 81 patients versus controls (SF-36 mental component 41.9 versus 46.1, P=0.006; EQ-5D extreme anxiety/depression 13.5 percent versus 2.2 percent, P<0.0001, PMID 18766120), the international survey of 720 individuals (secondary form worst on anxiety and depression; undiagnosed-group counterweight, PMID 41546369), and the 210-patient cross-sectional regression study (depression contributing 32 percent quality-of-life variance; anxiety contributing 23 percent symptom-severity variance in the REVERSE direction, PMID 38282510), with within-batch sharing across the pair recorded openly. The direction-inversion, shared-substrate (secondary Raynaud's carries connective-tissue-disease mood morbidity), survey-measure, and undiagnosed-counterweight limits are carried openly on both edges. Eighth evidence-preserving refusal recorded on the file: digital-ulcer disease has no catalog target identity.

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Raynaud's phenomenon associates with depressive symptoms at controlled primary-cohort and international-survey level: the controlled primary-Raynaud cohort of 81 patients versus control subjects documents a significantly lower SF-36 mental component score (41.9 plus or minus 9.4 versus 46.1 plus or minus 10.7, P=0.006) and far more extreme anxiety/depression on the EQ-5D (13.5 percent versus 2.2 percent, P<0.0001) with the psychological wellbeing domain the most involved area (PMID 18766120), the international survey of 720 individuals documents higher anxiety and depression scores in Raynaud's groups with the secondary form worst (PMID 41546369), and the 210-patient cross-sectional study documents depression contributing independently to quality-of-life variance alongside Raynaud's type and anxiety sensitivity (32 percent variance explained) (PMID 38282510); recorded as documented association only with the direction-inversion, shared-substrate, and survey-measure limits carried openly - psychological stress triggers and predicts episode severity within the same literature (anxiety explaining 23 percent of hand-symptom-severity variance), secondary Raynaud's carries the connective-tissue-disease mood burden, and the survey's undiagnosed comparison group paradoxically reported worse mental health than diagnosed groups.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of depressive-disorder is established for any individual: the same literature documents the reverse direction (emotional stress is a recognized episode trigger and anxiety predicts symptom severity so psychological state commonly precedes and amplifies the vasospasm), secondary Raynaud's patients carry their underlying connective-tissue disease which independently produces mood morbidity (shared substrate), the mood instruments are screening questionnaires (EQ-5D, DASS-21) rather than structured diagnoses, the controlled cohort is rheumatology-referred and small (81 patients), the international survey's undiagnosed comparison group reported worse mental health than the diagnosed groups which undercuts a simple exposure arrow, and individual claims require dated psychiatric assessment with pre-existing mood disorder, connective-tissue-disease activity, medication effects, and adjustment disorder excluded.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Chronic cold-triggered vasospastic attacks with pain, sleep disruption, and functional limitation are hypothesized to erode mood regulation over time, while stress-triggered amplification of vasospasm runs the route in reverse as well, the bidirectional psychophysiological coupling supported by the controlled primary-Roy mental-health deficit and the regression structure of the 210-patient study, but whether the forward route produced any individual's depressive episode remains hypothesized until psychiatric and vascular timelines are reviewed side by side.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association rests on one controlled 81-patient primary-Raynaud cohort plus one 720-person international survey plus one 210-patient cross-sectional study: mood outcomes are questionnaire-screened (EQ-5D, DASS-21) rather than diagnosed, the direction is contested within the same sources (stress and anxiety predict episode severity), secondary Raynaud's mood burden is inseparable from connective-tissue-disease substrate, the survey's undiagnosed group finding (worse mental health than diagnosed groups) is a direct counterweight to the exposure framing, and no longitudinal incident-depression cohort among Raynaud's patients free of mood disorder at baseline was located.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No longitudinal incident-depression cohort among Raynaud's phenomenon patients free of mood disorder at baseline was located; the controlled anchor (81 primary-Raynaud patients) measures SF-36 mental component and EQ-5D anxiety/depression items rather than diagnosed depressive-disorder; the 720-person survey's undiagnosed comparison group reported worse mental health than diagnosed groups (counterweight carried openly); anxiety predicting episode severity leaves direction contested; and secondary-Roy cohorts are substrate-confounded by their connective-tissue disease.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: connective-tissue disease (systemic sclerosis, lupus, rheumatoid arthritis) producing both secondary Raynaud's and independent mood morbidity (shared-substrate limit carried openly)
pre-existing mood disorder antedating the vasospastic syndrome (individual claims require documented pre-morbid psychiatric history)
cold-climate, occupational, and psychosocial stressors acting on both mood and vasospasm
medication effects including beta-blockers, vasoconstrictors, and mood-active agents; substance use including nicotine

evidenceGaps: No longitudinal incident-depression cohort among Raynaud's phenomenon patients free of mood disorder at baseline was located; the controlled anchor (81 primary-Raynaud patients) measures SF-36 mental component and EQ-5D anxiety/depression items rather than diagnosed depressive-disorder; the 720-person survey's undiagnosed comparison group reported worse mental health than diagnosed groups (counterweight carried openly); anxiety predicting episode severity leaves direction contested; and secondary-Roy cohorts are substrate-confounded by their connective-tissue disease.
suggestions.rationale: Authored at ASSOCIATION_ONLY at controlled-primary-cohort class with the direction-inversion, shared-substrate, and survey-measure limits carried openly, following the PSYCHOPHYSIOLOGICAL mood-edge convention: the controlled primary-Raynaud cohort documents the mental-health deficit against matched controls (PMID 18766120), the international survey documents the depression gradient across Raynaud's groups (PMID 41546369), and the regression study documents depression's independent contribution to quality-of-life variance (PMID 38282510), all carrying within-batch sharing with the anxiety edge; because the same literature documents stress-triggered reverse direction and the undiagnosed-group counterweight, the conservative standard keeps the edge at association only with those limits stated on the record and routes individual claims through dated psychiatric and rheumatologic timelines with pre-existing mood disorder and connective-tissue-disease activity excluded.

sourceReferences.citation: De Angelis R, Salaffi F, Grassi W. Health-related quality of life in primary Raynaud phenomenon J Clin Rheumatol. 2008 Aug;14(4):206-10. PMID 18766120.
sourceReferences.note: Controlled primary Raynaud phenomenon cohort (J Clin Rheumatol 2008): 81 patients versus control subjects; SF-36 mental component score 41.9 +/- 9.4 versus 46.1 +/- 10.7 (P=0.006); EQ-5D extreme anxiety/depression 13.5% versus 2.2% (P<0.0001); at-least-some anxiety/depression problems 77.7% versus 60.0% (P=0.005); psychological wellbeing the most involved area; supports the bounded association only (screening instruments, small referred cohort).

sourceReferences.citation: Irving D, Daniels J. Psychological factors in symptom severity and quality of life in Raynaud's phenomenon Behav Cogn Psychother. 2024 Jul;52(4):426-439. PMID 38282510.
sourceReferences.note: Cross-sectional psychological-factors study (Behav Cogn Psychother 2024): 210 adults with Raynaud's; depression, Raynaud's type, and anxiety sensitivity explained 32% of quality-of-life variance (p<0.001); anxiety explained 23% of hand-symptom-severity variance - the reverse direction carried openly (psychological factors predict episode severity); supports the bounded association only (cross-sectional, direction contested).

nexusClaim.associationBasis: Raynaud's phenomenon associates with anxiety symptoms at controlled primary-cohort and international-survey level: the controlled primary-Raynaud cohort of 81 patients versus controls documents significantly more anxiety/depression burden on the EQ-5D (77.7 percent reporting at least some problems versus 60.0 percent, P=0.005) with psychological wellbeing the most involved SF-36 area (PMID 18766120), the international survey of 720 individuals documents higher anxiety scores in Raynaud's groups with the secondary form worst (PMID 41546369), and the 210-patient cross-sectional study documents anxiety differing between primary and secondary types (P<0.004) and explaining 23 percent of hand-symptom-severity variance (PMID 38282510); recorded as documented association only with the direction-inversion limit carried prominently open - within the same literature anxiety predicts and stress triggers the vasospastic episodes so psychological state commonly precedes rather than follows the syndrome, sources are shared with the depressive-disorder edge within this batch.
nexusClaim.causationStatus: Neither causation nor aggravation of anxiety-disorder is established for any individual: the strongest directional signal in the located literature runs REVERSE (anxiety explains 23 percent of symptom-severity variance and emotional stress is a recognized episode trigger), secondary Raynaud's carries connective-tissue-disease substrate with independent anxiety morbidity (shared substrate), the instruments are screening questionnaires (EQ-5D, DASS-21) rather than structured diagnoses, autonomic arousal of anxiety overlaps the vasospastic physiology, and individual claims require dated psychiatric assessment with pre-existing anxiety disorder, connective-tissue-disease activity, medication effects, and adjustment disorder excluded.

causalMechanism.primaryVector: Anticipatory anxiety about cold exposure and painful attacks is hypothesized to condition hypervigilance and avoidance that sustains anxiety symptoms, while stress-triggered vasospasm amplification runs the coupling in reverse, the bidirectional route supported by the regression structure of the 210-patient study, but whether the forward route produced any individual's anxiety disorder remains hypothesized until psychiatric and vascular timelines are reviewed side by side.

evidentiaryProfile.conservativeRationale: The association rests on the same three cross-sectional anchors shared with the depressive-disorder edge: the direction-inversion is the dominant signal in the located literature (anxiety predicting severity, stress triggering episodes), autonomic arousal overlaps vasospastic physiology, secondary-Raynaud cohorts are substrate-confounded, the mood instruments are screening tools, and no longitudinal incident-anxiety cohort among Raynaud's patients free of anxiety at baseline was located.
evidentiaryProfile.evidenceGaps: No longitudinal incident-anxiety cohort among Raynaud's phenomenon patients free of anxiety at baseline was located; the quantified signals are screening-questionnaire scores (EQ-5D, DASS-21) in cross-sectional designs; anxiety predicting episode severity (23% severity variance) leaves direction contested in the forward-inverting sense; and the shared anchors are carried with the depressive-disorder edge within this batch.
alternativeEtiologiesToRuleOut: connective-tissue disease producing both secondary Raynaud's and independent anxiety morbidity (shared-substrate limit carried openly)
pre-existing anxiety disorder antedating the vasospastic syndrome (individual claims require documented pre-morbid psychiatric history)
autonomic arousal physiology overlapping vasospasm triggers (cold, stress)
stimulant, beta-blocker, and vasoconstrictor medication effects; nicotine and caffeine

evidenceGaps: No longitudinal incident-anxiety cohort among Raynaud's phenomenon patients free of anxiety at baseline was located; the quantified signals are screening-questionnaire scores (EQ-5D, DASS-21) in cross-sectional designs; anxiety predicting episode severity (23% severity variance) leaves direction contested in the forward-inverting sense; and the shared anchors are carried with the depressive-disorder edge within this batch.
